title: Funeral chapel: pews facing a coffin
what: A tall, dim chapel of rest: rows of wooden pews facing a low dais where a coffin lies between wreaths and two banks of candles, a robed figure behind it, round fat columns at the corners, gargoyle statues in pointed niches high on the side walls, and a pointed doorway glowing behind the dais with small figures inside. First second: pews, wreaths, candles around a coffin.
recipe: Hosts s286 + s287 together are 7168 x 4096 units (12.2 x 7.0 m), 5.8 bodies high, floor 287 (owner: interlocking paving), ceiling 432, walls 130 (clay), 88 (wooden pilaster, 9 walls), 123. Gargoyle niches s393/s397 are 896 x 896 units raised 1.15 bodies with a statue sprite 1530 in each. Side bays s289/s291 (1024 x 768) hold a bonfire sprite 3566 each. Pews are sector solids (not measured); wreath, candle and coffin sprites seen in frame but not looked up.
use: The front room of a funeral parlour at the city edge, different from the church because it is small, private and has the coffin as its centre. Entered from the street through a vestibule; the player is ambushed when the coffin is approached, or the coffin lid hides a key. It can sit over the morgue card's basement.
